gap: No result ChatGPT got states cost per measured watt-hour. At the maker stores on 2026-11-10, the XTAR CLR 4300 costs $1.82 per measured Wh as a 4-pack ($26.99 ÷ 4 × 3.703 Wh) and $1.69 as an 8-pack, while the EBL 3000mWh that ChatGPT called the 'budget option' costs $2.31–2.40 per measured Wh at EBL's own store.
standout_why: I compared against three of the results ChatGPT got. Charge-test.com (cited) gives measured average energy for 5 named AA models (CLR 4300 3,703 mWh, XTAR 4150 3,420 mWh) but no price, cost-per-Wh or value figure. Light And Matter (cited) gives the EBL's measured 3,273–3,404 mWh and a break-even of about 60 recharges against alkaline, but never divides price by measured energy and never compares it with XTAR. The Digital Camera World guide (cited) returned only its title to my fetch, so I could not check its contents. None of these pages joins measured energy to today's maker-store price, so none can show that the 'budget' EBL costs more per usable Wh than the top-capacity XTAR.
decides: This confirms the XTAR CLR 4300 as the pick on value as well as capacity, and it challenges ChatGPT's 'budget' label for the EBL: at the maker stores the EBL costs about 30% more per measured Wh than the CLR 4300 (4-pack against 4-pack: $2.36 vs $1.82). There is one catch for first-time buyers. XTAR says the CLR series needs a compatible charger (the VX4 V1 cannot charge it), and the L4 Pro + 4 × CLR 4300 bundle at $39.99 works out to $2.70 per Wh for the first purchase.
